leadText: Kotarō (Japanese: コタロウ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest.
plainText:
Kotarō (Japanese: コタロウ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest.

==In the games==

===Warlord information===
When Kotarō enters a battle, there is a chance that a wild may appear, disguised as a duplicate of one of the wild Pokémon shown in the battle preview. This is the only way for wild Zorua to spawn without the use of .

====Rank I====
 

====Rank II====
 

Transforms to Rank II by reaching a 60% link with Zorua or Zoroark.

===Quotes===
Start of turn:
When asleep:
"Hm... Sleeping..."
With low health or a status ailment: 
"The situation is...delicate..."
When victory is near:
"Let's finish them..."
Otherwise: 
"Go..."

Start of battle:
When attacking a castle: 
"Throw them into oblivion."
When defending a castle: 
"They must want to be crushed..."

During battle: 
"Not a bad battle at all, is it, ? Let's stir things up as best we can..."

When ordering to attack: 
" ..."

When ordering to go to battle: 
To a kingdom:
"Ha... I can already tell you how this battle will end..."
To a wild Pokémon location:
"Let's have some fun..."

Upon forming a link: 
"I have formed a link with ..."

When using an item: 
" ..."

When using his Warrior Skill: 
"Let's shake things up..."

After winning a battle: 
If he attacked a castle:
"That was far too easy..."
If he defended a castle:
"Feeling bitter...? Hehe..."

When defeated:
If recruitable:
"Hehe... I've taken a liking to you..."
If defeated by something other than the enemy:
"Ha... How amusing."
Otherwise:
"Fun's over..."

When being recruited:
"Fine. Let's see how you fare..."

At the start of :
"Ha... This will be enjoyable."

===Profile===
A ninja who seems set on throwing all of Ransei into turmoil. His true motivations for doing so, however, remain a mystery to all.

==In the manga==
===Pokémon + Nobunaga's Ambition ~ Ranse's Color Picture Scroll ~===
Kotarō debuted in PNA4.
 
====Pokémon====
 

==Trivia==
Kotarō has the lowest Charisma of any Warlord.

===Historical origin===
Kotarō is based on the real-life of Japanese history. Isuke ( ) was of the Fūma clan as well. Kotarō served both Ujimasa ( ) and Ujinao ( ).
